The ListBox and ComboBox controls provide list boxes and drop-down list boxes that the user can scroll through to see options or pieces of information. List boxes can display multiple items, while drop-down list boxes can display one item at a time. However, the user can click the scroll arrow to display and scroll through a list of all the items in the list box.

> **Tip:** If you have space on the form and want to emphasize the choices the user can make, use a list. To conserve space and emphasize the currently selected item, use a drop-down list box.

You can fill a list box or combo box with items from a variety of sources by setting the RowSourceType Property and RowSource Property properties. For more information, see How to: Choose the Type of Data for a List or Combo Box.

[[T0]] drag-and-drop support is available at run time for [[T1]] controls and the text editor. The controls and the text editor support [[T2]] drag-and-drop interactively at run time, and the controls provide programmatic support at run time. The DataObject Object provides programmatic [[T3]] drag-and-drop support for the controls.

Two modes of [[T4]] drag-and-drop are available for [[T5]] controls: intrinsic mode and manual mode. In intrinsic mode, [[T6]] intrinsically handles an [[T7]] drag-and-drop operation. In manual mode, [[T8]] drag-and-drop operations are handled programmatically. The events that occur are determined by the [[T9]] drag-and-drop mode. For more information, see the section, "Intrinsic and Manual [[T10]] drag-and-drop Modes."

Previous versions of [[T0]] supported programmatic drag-and-drop for controls, making it possible for you to move controls on a form. This form of drag and drop is still supported. If you use the default settings for the OLEDragMode and OLEDropMode properties, your existing applications will run as before without any changes.

The DataObject Object is a container for data being transferred from an [[T0]] drag source to an [[T1]] drop target, and exists only for the duration of an [[T2]] drag-and-drop operation. The DataObject object cannot be created programmatically and references to it become invalid once the [[T3]] drag-and-drop operation is completed. The DataObject is passed as the [[T4]] parameter in the OLEStartDrag, OLEDragOver, OLEDragDrop, and OLESetData events.

The DataObject can store multiple sets of data, each in a different format. The existence of a specific format in the DataObject can be determined with the GetFormat method. See the GetFormat Method for a listing of the formats supported by the DataObject.

The DataObject object has methods that make it possible for you to programmatically manipulate the data being dragged and dropped. The following table lists the methods available at run time for the DataObject.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ClearData | Clears all data and data formats from the [[T0]] drag-and-drop DataObject object. |
| GetData | Retrieves data from the [[T1]] drag-and-drop DataObject object. |
| GetFormat | Determines whether data in a specified format is available on the [[T2]] drag-and-drop DataObject. |
| SetData | Places data and its format on the [[T3]] drag-and-drop DataObject. |
| SetFormat | Places a data format without data on the [[T4]] drag-and-drop DataObject. |
